Architecture Diagram

ContosoUniversity is a single web application for managing university students, instructors, courses, departments, and enrollment records. Its MVC controllers use an EF Core context for SQL Server access and enqueue notifications through Microsoft Message Queuing.

Data Storage & External Services

The application uses a SQL Server connection configured in Web.config (currently LocalDB with integrated security) for domain and notification entities. It also uses a local private MSMQ queue to carry serialized notifications. No separately deployed APIs, caches, or external service endpoints were identified.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Uses conventional ASP.NET MVC controllers and Razor views in a single deployable web application.
  • Creates an EF Core SchoolContext for controller operations and initializes seed data at application startup.
  • Sends CRUD notifications through MSMQ rather than through an external service or persistent event broker.

DTOs & Contracts

MVC actions primarily bind directly to domain model classes (Student, Course, Instructor, and Department) and return Razor views. AssignedCourseData, InstructorIndexData, and EnrollmentDateGroup are view models used to shape page data. Notification endpoints serialize Notification records into JSON; no immutable request/response DTOs, OpenAPI definition, GraphQL schema, or protobuf schema was found. JSON serialization uses Newtonsoft.Json in the queue service and MVC JSON results for notification responses.

Communication Patterns

Browser-to-application communication uses HTTP through the conventional MVC route. Controllers synchronously call SchoolContext and EF Core for database operations. CRUD notifications are serialized and sent to MSMQ; the notification controller later receives them during a request, so there is no separate API call or distributed service choreography. No retry policy, circuit breaker, timeout policy, service discovery, or API gateway was identified. The connection string uses LocalDB integrated security. Web.config enables Windows authentication in IIS Express and disables anonymous authentication, but controller actions do not declare explicit authorization attributes; no TLS deployment policy was identified in the project configuration.

Core Business Workflows

ContosoUniversity supports school administration: staff maintain student, instructor, course, and department records, and associate students with courses. Changes are reflected in the database and published as notifications for the dashboard.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
ContosoUniversityUniversity administration and curriculum managementPerson, Student, Instructor, Course, Department, Enrollment, CourseAssignment, OfficeAssignment, NotificationSQL Server and MSMQ

The application is a single service with one source of truth in SQL Server. Domains exchange data through shared EF Core relationships rather than remote APIs or events between separate services.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Register a Student

  1. A staff user opens the student creation page and supplies student information.
  2. The controller applies model validation and checks that the enrollment date is within the SQL Server-supported range.
  3. If validation succeeds, the controller saves the Student through SchoolContext.
  4. The controller sends a Student-created notification and redirects to the student list.
  5. If validation fails, the form is returned with validation messages; if persistence fails, a diagnostic entry is recorded and the user receives a generic error.

Workflow 2: Assign Courses to an Instructor

  1. A staff user submits the instructor form with selected course identifiers.
  2. The controller builds CourseAssignment records for the selected courses.
  3. On edit, the controller compares selected courses with existing assignments, adds new relationships, and removes deselected relationships.
  4. The context saves the instructor and assignment changes, then sends a notification and redirects.

Workflow 3: Review Notifications

  1. The dashboard requests pending notifications.
  2. NotificationsController reads from the notification queue, stopping after ten messages or a receive timeout.
  3. The controller returns the results as JSON for the page to display.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no independently deployed application services or cross-service composition flows. Controllers query the shared database through SchoolContext. CRUD notifications are sent to MSMQ and later consumed by the notification endpoint; if the queue is empty, the service returns no notification and the dashboard receives an empty list.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Staff as "Staff User" participant Controller as "StudentsController" participant Context as "SchoolContext" participant DB as "SQL Server" participant Notify as "NotificationService" participant Queue as "MSMQ Queue" Staff->>Controller: Submit student details Controller->>Controller: Validate model and enrollment date alt Input is valid Controller->>Context: Add student Context->>DB: Save student record DB-->>Context: Save completed Context-->>Controller: Persisted student Controller->>Notify: Publish student-created event Notify-->>Queue: Enqueue notification Controller-->>Staff: Redirect to student list else Input is invalid Controller-->>Staff: Return form with validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Student enrollment dates must be supplied and fall within the supported SQL Server datetime range.
  • Course image uploads are limited by the controller to a set of common image filename extensions and a maximum size of 5 MB.
  • Instructor course assignments are synchronized to the selected course list; deselected relationships are removed.
  • Department edits use a row-version value to detect concurrent updates and return conflict information when the record changes concurrently.
  • Create, update, and delete actions publish entity notifications after database writes. Notification failures are handled without cancelling the underlying business operation.
  • Student and instructor names and enrollment/grade information are education-related personal data. No separate workflow-level masking behavior was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.8 and uses ASP.NET MVC 5.2.9 and EF Core 3.1.32, a legacy framework/library combination with migration compatibility work likely required. EF Core 3.1 is out of support. The declared Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 version is affected by CVE-2024-0056; the advisory lists 2.1.7 as the first patched version in the applicable range.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config is the package manifest; versions are pinned per package rather than centrally managed.
  • Several EF Core and Microsoft.Extensions.* packages are individually declared at 3.1.32.
  • The project declares packages such as Microsoft Identity Client but does not show corresponding use in the application source.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application stores university people, courses, departments, enrollment records, and notifications in SQL Server through EF Core. Its model includes shared-table inheritance for people and an explicit join entity for instructor/course assignments.

SchoolContext configures Person using table-per-hierarchy inheritance, a composite key for CourseAssignment, and a one-to-one relationship between Instructor and OfficeAssignment. Enrollment relates students and courses. The context configures date-time properties as SQL Server datetime2.

Caching Strategy

No application-level cache, distributed cache, query-result cache, or cache TTL configuration was identified. EF Core tracks entities within each context lifetime; controllers create and dispose their contexts per request.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The application uses a single shared SQL Server database and one EF Core context; there are no independently deployed services or service-to-service database calls. Controllers query and update the same context directly. Instructor-to-course associations are represented by CourseAssignment, while student/course associations are represented by Enrollment; no CQRS or cross-service aggregation pattern was found.
